newsitem.title: ROMANIA: British Petroleum in $8.0 mln Romania deal.
newsitem.headline: British Petroleum in $8.0 mln Romania deal.

text.p: Romania's state airline Tarom SA signed on Thursday an accord with Air BP, British Petroleum Co Plc's aviation fuel's arm, to set up a joint venture and bring fuelling on Romanian airports to Western standards.
"The project is worth some $8.0 million," Air BP's regional manager Howard Dewey told Reuters.

Under the accord, BP would ensure funds for the project and supply fuelling equipment, including big capacity tanker vehicles and storage facilities, he said, adding that in the first stage, Air BP would also provide the new company with expertise and management.
The new venture is expected to become operational by August. Both Tarom and BP would have a 50 percent stake in the new venture, Tarom general manager Dan Vulcan said.

The first stage of the project would target Bucharest's international airport Otopeni, he said. Eventually, the project would expand to the western airport of Timisoara and to the Constanta airport, on the Black Sea coast.
The new facilities would help Tarom cut both operations costs and delays on its scheduled flights.
"There were cases when we had to delay some of our international flights by up to four hours due to the shortage of proper fuelling equipment," he said.
